name: אֲחִימוֹת
gloss: brother of death; or my brother is death
summary: A Levite of the sons of Kohath, a son of Elkanah and brother of Amasai in the line that leads to Samuel, named once. As the Hebrew writes it, the name is אֲחִי, “brother of” or “my brother”, joined to מוֹת, the construct of מָוֶת “death”, formed as the other names in אֲחִי־ are (Ahiezer, “my brother is help”). Scripture does not explain it. The second list of the same line has מַחַת, Mahath, in this place (1Ch 6:20), so the name may be another form of that one, and its tie to this root rests on the spelling alone.

evidence.note: “The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and אֲחִימוֹת.”
The same line traced upward: “son of Elkanah, son of Mahath (מַחַת), son of Amasai”.
אֲחִיעֶזֶר, a name of the same form.
מוֹת as the construct of מָוֶת: “the death of the high priest”.

note: TIPNR keys him by the English verse numbering (1Ch 6:25); the Hebrew verse is 1Ch 6:10. TIPNR identifies him with Mahath of 1Ch 6:20 (English 6:35). The database files the key a.ck.an under אחה; the ach entry leaves the אֲחִי־ names to their second element's root. Whether מוֹת here is “death” or a worn form of another word (compare Mahath) is not settled by any verse.
